protections: P1 folder capability: a folder's dirkey (and the dirkeys of its subfolders) may only be emitted to a caller who already holds folder-level access to that folder - read permission, or that folder's own dirkey (enforced correctly at the ?tree= emitter via the will_read flag, httpcli.py:5874-5890,5910-5917, but not at the browser listing emitter, httpcli.py:7207-7215,7254-7259,7304-7308).

P2 file capability: a filekey may only be emitted for a file the caller can already fetch - read, the folder's dirkey, its own filekey, or upget/uploader status (httpcli.py:2775-2784, 3975-3984, 7293-7303; up2k.py:3493-3503).

P3 file fetch without read: a caller without read may fetch a file only with a valid filekey, or through the documented exemptions - index.html for permission 'h' (httpcli.py:6912-6940), share paths (httpcli.py:6948), or a valid dirkey for the containing folder (httpcli.py:6840-6848,6942-6950).

conflicts.what: A guard written as 'only emit dk to callers with read' (the obvious reading of the advisory) suppresses the dks subfolder dirkeys at httpcli.py:7304-7308, which dirkey callers need and tests/test_dots.py:319-327 assert; the guard has to be 'can_read or use_dirkey'.

Refusing the ?v viewer (or dropping keys) for non-read callers breaks the filekey echo into og_thumb/og_raw (httpcli.py:7671-7684) and the filekey hotlinks a dirkey listing must keep (httpcli.py:7293-7303, tests/test_dots.py:311-313).

The cleanest T4 fix (stop copying dk/dks onto share nodes at authsrv.py:3181) also strips the dks subfolder navigation that a legitimate folder share relies on (httpcli.py:7304-7308), so the fix has to distinguish single-file shares (shr_files set, authsrv.py:3166) from folder shares.

Closing T2 by clearing add_og at httpcli.py:6940 changes the response for an 'h' user fetching index.html with ?v from the opengraph page to the raw file; the documented behaviour (README.md:544,3066) only promises index.html without a filekey, so the fix must keep returning index.html.

fairness_risks: A rule that denies the opengraph view to callers without read contradicts the documented og/og_ua feature (README.md:1639-1645), whose whole purpose is link previews for shared file URLs.

A rule that refuses ?k=<filekey>&v refuses the documented combination of filekeys and opengraph (docs/changelog.md:2488) and the medialinks uploader link, which appends &v to a ?k= URL (httpcli.py:2775-2787).
A rule that requires read to receive any key breaks the dirkeys feature itself: dirkey recipients never have read (README.md:3106-3114, httpcli.py:4314-4317).
A rule that suppresses filekeys in a dirkey listing breaks hotlinking from a dirkey-shared folder (README.md:3116; tests/test_dots.py:289-293,311-313).
A rule that requires a key for index.html contradicts the documented 'h' permission semantics (README.md:544,3066, docs/changelog.md:3839).
A rule that drops dk from share nodes entirely breaks dks navigation for folder shares.

design.why: Three independent judgements, five route-level tests. (1) T1/T2/T3 are one missing check at one site (httpcli.py:7207-7215) but three entry conditions with three different dismissal arguments: a validated filekey (T1, the advisory), the documented index.html-without-a-filekey exemption for 'h' (T2), and a dks volume with no fk that the docs call ill-advised (T3). The published one-liner ('not use_filekey') closes only T1, so a solver who reproduces it fails the two keyless routes; the correct predicate is folder-level authorization ('can_read or use_dirkey'), which the ?tree= emitter already uses at httpcli.py:5874-5890. This is the deepseek-type core: protection absent plus a plausible reason to dismiss. (2) T4 is independent of that guard because a single-file share with 'r' sets can_read from the share grant while the emitter's key is for the source folder: the producer (authsrv.py:3181 copies the source volume's dk/dks/fk onto every share node) is the only place the two can be told apart, so it is a separate fix site and a separate judgement. (3) T5 is the mimo-type constraint: the fix must not over-harden - it has to keep filekeys in a dirkey listing, subfolder dirkeys under dks, and the filekey embedded in og_thumb/og_raw, all asserted in tests/test_dots.py:289-293,311-313,319-327. The stack is real but thin: 75% of it can be closed by one corrected predicate, so the hidden tests must include at least one keyless route and one share case for the stacking to bite.
